name: Gajim
description: App updater is notify-only (TLS-verified). But plugin installer fetches ZIPs over TLS with zero hash/signature, then extractall()'s + loads as Python — content-as-code. gajim.org/CDN compromise ⇒ arbitrary code.
limitations: AI-generated static source analysis. Confirm the affected version, platform, update channel, and cited control flow before relying on this classification.

later_review_audit.description: Gajim's core check fetches a version JSON and opens the external download page; the app does not download or execute an installer.
limitations: Newly retrieved source snapshot at the recorded commit; this is not historical release re-verification. Released artifact behavior and external framework enforcement remain unverified.
This is a newly retrieved default-branch snapshot, not the original study checkout; canonical release behavior is not established.

original_evidence.text: | Gajim | https://dev.gajim.org/gajim/gajim.git | 772f2a8a / 2026-08-11 | Y (notify-only) | N (opens browser link only) | N (core updater) / **Y (plugin installer, separate channel — see below)** | https, TLS validation ENFORCED | N/A | none | N/A | Core self-update check: `gajim/common/application.py:296-320` `check_for_gajim_updates()` → `app.ftm.http_request("GET","https://gajim.org/current-version.json", …)`; response handled in `_on_update_response` (`application.py:322-345`) which just compares versions and raises `GajimUpdateAvailable`. Consumer at `gajim/gtk/activity_page.py:181` does `open_uri(event.setup_url)` — opens the download page in the default browser; **no download or execution of any installer happens in-app**. Transport: `gajim/common/multiprocess/http.py:153-156` builds `httpx.Client(verify=ctx, …)` where `ctx = truststore.SSLContext(...)` (OS trust store) — cert validation is enforced, no `verify=False`/`InsecureSkipVerify` found anywhere in the module. |
